newsitem.title: HUNGARY: LAWMAKERS IN HUNGARY FINED FOR ABSENTEEISM.
newsitem.headline: LAWMAKERS IN HUNGARY FINED FOR ABSENTEEISM.

text.p: Six members of Hungary's ruling Socialist Party will receive smaller paycheques next month for skipping parliamentary sessions, a Socialist official said on Thursday.
"The system has been in effect for a year and a half and the number of penalised (Socialist) MPs is usually very small," Peter Szeredi, head of the Socialist caucus's office told Reuters.
Lawmakers who cannot justify their absence from more than one third of the votes in any given month are fined a proportional part of their salary.
National daily Nepszabadsag reported on Thursday that Socialist MP and affluent businessman Laszlo Mate will only receive 39 percent of next month's salary for skipping sessions.
The monthly gross wage of Hungary's MPs -- allowances not included -- amounts to 114,000 forints compared with a national average of 51,510 forints.
